title: Centrus sends first new centrifuge built at Oak Ridge to Piketon plant
summary: On October 29, representatives from Centrus Energy Corp. joined government officials for a press event to commemorate the completion and shipment of the first centrifuge built for the expansion of the company’s Piketon, Ohio, uranium enrichment plant. Speaking at the Centrus Technology and Manufacturing Center in Oak Ridge, Tenn., Amir Vexler, the company’s president and CEO, said, “This may sound like a simple shipment from one facility to another, but it represents something much larger. It connects American manufacturing in Tennessee and American uranium enrichment in Ohio . . and it demonstrates that Centrus has assembled the specialized people capability and domestic supply chain to build this technology at scale.”

title: UW-Madison breaks ground on new radioisotope cyclotron facility
summary: The University of Wisconsin–Madison School of Medicine and Public Health has broken ground on a project to add two cyclotrons to its existing medical research infrastructure, increasing the university’s radioisotope production capacity by two- to eightfold, depending on the particular isotope. The $62 million project—funded by the National Institutes of Health, the Wisconsin Alumni Research Foundation, and private donations—is expected to be completed by May 2028. The new 13,000-square-foot facility, which is being built within the Wisconsin Institutes for Medical Research complex, is slated to host “the first modern alpha-particle cyclotron of its kind installed in the United States,” according to the university.

title: NN announces the 2026 40 Under 40 honorees
summary: The Nuclear News 40 Under 40 is back for a third year, and with this class the list has now recognized 120 young professionals who are helping shape the future of the nuclear enterprise. What began as an experiment in 2024 is now an annual tradition. Reviewing the stacks of stellar nominations has been a difficult but satisfying task for the editorial team as we create the final list, published in the November issue of Nuclear News.
